title: All 14 Indians Aboard Yacht Off Yemen Reported Safe Around Hodeidah
excerpt: India's embassy in Yemen said Friday all 14 nationals are safe near Hodeidah, a day after the Houthis claimed Saudi forces targeted their boat near the Bab el-Mandeb.
body:
• All 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off Yemen's coast are reported safe and located around Hodeidah, the Indian embassy in Yemen said Friday.
  • The update follows Thursday's Houthi claim that Saudi forces targeted the boat near Jabal Zuqar island by the Bab el-Mandeb strait and that Houthi forces were rescuing those aboard.
  • Saudi authorities had not responded to a Reuters request for comment on Thursday; the circumstances of the October 22 incident remain unconfirmed.
  • India is the world's third-largest supplier of seafarers, with over 300,000 sailors in global fleets — families should follow the Indian embassy in Yemen for verified updates on the group's return.

All 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off Yemen's coast are reported safe, the Indian embassy in Yemen said on Friday, in the first confirmed update on their condition since the incident on October 22.

"Reports suggest that all 14 Indian nationals are safe and located around Hodeidah in Yemen. We will continue to work for ensuring their well being," the embassy said in a post on X, according to Reuters reporting on the embassy statement. The embassy had earlier said precise information was not available and that it was attempting to establish the circumstances and facts of the incident.

"Reports suggest that all 14 Indian nationals are safe and located around Hodeidah in Yemen. We will continue to work for ensuring their well being."

— Indian Embassy in Yemen, via X

From a Houthi claim to a confirmed update

The story entered public view on Thursday through a claim, not a confirmation. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they were rescuing a boat carrying 14 Indians that was attacked off Jabal Zuqar island near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree posted that Saudi forces were targeting an Indian yacht near Zuqar Island, that Yemeni Armed Forces were rescuing those aboard, and that the alleged act threatened international navigation in the Red Sea, according to Bizz Buzz coverage of the embassy and Houthi statements.

https://x.com/WIONews/status/2113547185791078628

Saudi authorities did not respond to a Reuters request for comment on Thursday. No independent account has yet established who, if anyone, attacked the vessel, or exactly what happened on October 22. Friday's embassy statement confirms the group's safety and location around Hodeidah, a Red Sea port city. It does not describe injuries, the vessel's condition, or the timeline for their onward travel.

A dangerous week for Indians in the region

The yacht incident came a day after an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, on October 21, in which an Indian national was among two people killed and two other Indian nationals were injured, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said. India's Ministry of External Affairs on Thursday strongly condemned continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the Dammam airport attack and a strike on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field, calling the attacks "completely unacceptable" and expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

Reuters noted that more than a dozen Indian seafarers have been killed and three are missing in the Gulf and the wider West Asian maritime region since the Middle East conflict began in February. India is the world's third-largest supplier of seafarers, with more than 300,000 sailors working across global shipping fleets, according to government data — a scale that puts Indian crews on vessels throughout the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth where Houthi forces and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government have clashed.

What happens next

The embassy said it will continue to work to ensure the 14 nationals' well-being. It has not yet announced arrangements for their return to India or release of their names. Until a fuller official account is published, the verified facts are narrow but reassuring: an incident occurred off Yemen on October 22, a rescue was claimed by the Houthis on Thursday, and on Friday India's embassy reported all 14 safe around Hodeidah. Families and employers should rely on embassy updates rather than competing claims about responsibility, which remain unconfirmed.
